headline.production: Production is still dead: both old Railway addresses answer Railway's own 404. Nine phases are merged on GitHub (P1, P2a, P3a, P6a, P7a, P8a, P9-0a, P12a, L2); none is deployed, because nothing reaches a server or a phone before your pre-flight.
headline.critical: Your pre-flight (P0a) has not started. It is the critical path: nothing reaches a phone or a server until it is done. Its first two answers are already needed: the domain name you will use, and the highest app version number on any technician's phone. The drain tooling is built and reviewed and waits only for those two. New on 2026-11-14: GitHub has stopped running the automatic checks (billing: the month's included minutes are used up or a payment failed), so nothing more can be merged until you restore them or allow merging on this PC's own runs. I used far more of those minutes than I should have: every note I saved to the plan started a full run. That is stopped. Two new sessions are proposed and wait for your click on their cards: the web defects phase, which the drain needs, and the next money phase.

phases.name: Drain tooling and fleet profile (phone app)
phases.note: Built, and passed its independent review after three passes and 25 deliberate attempts to break it: no way was found to lose, duplicate or misattribute a technician's records. The phone app also compiles natively on this PC with its changes (checked twice, the second time on the final build settings). It is finished on our side and now waits for exactly two values from you: (1) the domain name you will use (it does not have to work yet), and (2) the highest app version number on any technician's phone. It cannot merge without them, and the rest of the drain path queues behind it. Update, 2026-11-14: the reviews of the audit script (P2b-2) showed the phone has to say a little more in its record list, so this phase was reopened for a small addition (ruling C39): an identifier per phone, and a second short report after the drain of what is still on the phone and why. Its reviewer reads the addition before anything merges. It still waits for your two values. The addition is built and reviewed (2026-11-14): everything the contract asks of the phone holds. One small fix remains (ruling C46): a voice clip a technician deletes must always leave a record of that, even when the phone's storage hiccups, so the audit never mistakes a deleted clip for a lost one. Two short re-reads later (rulings C48 and C50) the code is settled: a deleted clip is described truthfully, is not uploaded, and always leaves its record. Only a wording touch-up is left, and then it waits for your two values.

phases.name: Drain audit script (backend)
phases.note: This is the script that proves the drain is complete: it compares what each phone said it held with what reached the server, record by record, and its answer is what lets you move on. Because a wrong 'all accounted for' would lose real records, it had two independent reviews, and neither let it through as it was. The first found that when two technicians share a phone, one's action could be counted as proof that the other's unsent record had arrived, with nothing printed; and that in two situations it would report a problem no action could clear. The second found that it never writes to your data, never shows a password and does run on the pinned server image, but that it read the database in many small looks instead of one, so a phone uploading in the middle could trigger a false 'stop everything'. Money records held under both: matched one to one, never written off. I set one contract for the phone side and the script side (ruling C39). The main change you will notice: after the drain, each phone sends a short second report of what is still on it and why, so the script can tell 'still uploading', 'needs entering by hand' and 'lost' apart, and every answer comes with what to do about it. Both lanes are making the changes; each goes back to its reviewer. It merges after the drain tooling (P2b-1), so it too waits for your two values. Update, 04:35 on 2026-11-14: the lane reported its fix round done, with its own tests green. I have not sent it to review yet, because it was built before four of my later rulings reached it (its turn was long and my messages waited in line). I also settled two points with it. A record that a phone gave up on without any answer from our server is not 'enter it by hand': the script will say 'tap Retry on that phone first', because a record entered by hand while the phone can still send it would end up recorded twice, and for a payment that is cash counted twice. And the option that marks the field test's records can be used for one phone at a time only, and has to list every record it marks.

phases.name: Self-host repository changes
phases.note: Merged 2026-11-13 as 90ea88d after two independent review passes. It is everything the new server will run and the step-by-step runbook you will follow. The first review found four serious problems (the stand-in for the old address could answer on its own; a mistyped settings line could start the server in the wrong mode; one 'stop' step would have made every phone treat its records as refused; the restore deleted before it proved the backup). All four were fixed, and the reviewer repeated each attack and could no longer get through. Nothing is deployed: your server work (P3b) starts from this runbook once your pre-flight answers exist. The same evening its runbook section on cutting the pinned drain image was corrected in two reviewed steps (PRs #205 and #206, merged as 66e891b and 7bf9f49): it takes the timezone fix as the second of four commits, that commit is tagged so it cannot be lost, and the section now checks which commits were picked. A last correction (PR #207, merged 2026-11-14 as 53c6046) fixed the order of the final steps: the branch is pushed first, its automatic checks are read, and only then is the image tagged. Its review caught one real mistake on the way: the step for the web image would have tagged the backend commit. A larger batch of corrections to the restore, drain and backup steps (PR #209), from the rehearsal's findings, has had its first review: every correction does what it should, and the reviewer found one more gap of the same kind (a fallback path could still reach the delete step with only a damaged copy saved) and one that matters on a bad day: commands pasted through a hosting provider's emergency console could silently swallow the lines after them. Both are being fixed before it merges. Update: the batch's second review passed it with nothing left to fix (2026-11-14, at bcbf506). It merges once the rehearsal tool has typed the corrected steps end to end on its stand-in server, which is the second check I set for it. Not merged yet (06:17 on 2026-11-14): the rehearsal went through the corrected runbook with no failed step, but the tool skipped two of its steps, the one that sets the workshop's location and the one that sets the PINs, because their layout had changed. The commands in those two steps are the same as before, and the reviewer found nothing in them that could hurt your restore. I still hold the merge until the tool has run them from the corrected text: a step that was skipped was not rehearsed.

phases.name: Money integrity 1: void attribution, payloads
phases.note: Merged on 2026-11-14 as 16e154e, after three independent review passes. It records who voided a payment, when and why (the first database migration of this program), makes each payment and void its own event, and builds your decision: only a manager may record or void a payment on a closed job, with a written reason. Two rules of mine came out of its reviews: text a person types is never copied into the system's event record, and a payment never fails because of a phone's clock. The last review left two small points that no app in existence can reach; they are being fixed in a short follow-up, and that follow-up must be in before the new phone app is built. Nothing changes for the shop until this is deployed; when it is, its database change is applied and checked by the steps recorded in the deploy list. The manager screens still need a small change before a manager can use the closed-job rule from the web; that goes to the web phase. Update: that follow-up (PR #210) passed its review on 2026-11-14 with nothing left to fix. It is the first thing waiting on GitHub's stopped checks: it merges as soon as they run again, or on this PC's runs if you allow that.

Today's app compiles to an APK on this PC (24 minutes the first time, about 75 seconds after that), and the paid location kit (version 5.8.2) compiles on SDK 52. phases.name: Device lab (emulator on this PC)
phases.note: The first part (L3a) built the emulator, a local backend and a stand-in for the dead production host on this PC, and ran the first checks of today's app. Its independent review came back at 20:03. The safety question passed: no lab command can reach a real phone plugged into this PC. But four of its results did not match its own logs. The clearest: one known tracker defect was reported as not seen, while the log shows it happening three times out of three; and one check could never fail. They went back to be corrected and re-run, and no lab result is used to design the phone repair until the same reviewer has re-read them. The drain rehearsal on the emulator comes after that. The re-run was cut off when the PC shut down on the evening of 2026-11-13; the lab was restarted after the reboot and continues. Update: I paused the lab at 04:10 on 2026-11-14 and had its emulator stopped. Your own diagnosis that night showed what the freezes come from, and the emulator was the largest single thing of mine on the machine while two long test lanes were also running. It resumes when they are done, and from now on it never runs beside several test runs.

phases.name: Deploy-train and restore rehearsal
phases.note: It rehearsed, on this PC and against a stand-in database, the restore you will run by hand on the new server and the later deploy sequence, typing the runbook's own commands and trying deliberate wrong turns. Its independent review ran both rehearsals again and got the same results, confirmed its findings about the runbook, and found more. The ones that matter for you: one check would have stopped you at a perfectly good restore (and your real backup is almost certainly in exactly that state); the step that deletes and restores the database had no guard, so a failed safety backup, or simply a new terminal window, could have left you with an empty database and a restore that then fails; and one step needs a time that only the following step records. All of these go to the runbook's lane as one batch, and from now on the rehearsal can test a runbook change before it is merged, not after. The rehearsal tool itself goes back for fixes too: it must start from the pinned server image the way the real server will, so that the first database change in the deploy list is rehearsed properly. Separately it found the nightly jobs running five hours late (being fixed in the code). Update, 05:56 on 2026-11-14: the fixes are in. The tool now starts from the pinned server image, and it proves that its own checks can fail: 18 deliberate faults, one per kind of check, all caught. The first trial of that exposed one of its checks that could never have failed; it is fixed. It also rehearsed the corrected runbook before that correction is merged: the restore goes through with no failed step, where today's runbook fails at three. Two steps of the corrected runbook were not typed, because their layout changed in a way the tool refuses to guess at; that is being settled before the runbook correction merges. The second review has begun with the reading, and it will run the rehearsals itself once the session has stopped adding to them. The reading half of the second review is back (06:17): everything from the first review is fixed except one thing, and it found two serious points of its own. First, in some places the tool still picks a command by its position in a block instead of by what it says, and in one case that made it report eight safety checks as passed when it had not tried any of them. Second, two rehearsals started at the same time destroy each other and mix up their results. Both went straight back to the session, together with six smaller ones, so they are fixed in the same round.

p0a.title: Tools and access
p0a.do: Start Docker Desktop. Install Android platform-tools (adb), build-tools (apksigner) and a JDK. Log in: EAS, GitHub CLI, Railway CLI (only if you control the old Railway hostname). Check you can log in to the Railway, Supabase, Cloudflare, Sentry, Firebase and Expo dashboards. Turn on USB debugging on every roster phone. Have a cable and a spare Android phone (for P2c).
p0a.why: Every other item uses these. It is done first, before item 1.
p0a.helper: tools-check.sh. adb, apksigner and a JDK are already installed for you in C:/Users/User/.fixflow-cache/android/ (nothing was added to the system PATH: the first command below loads them into one terminal)
p0a.result: e.g. docker yes, adb yes, apksigner yes, JDK yes, logins 6/6, USB debugging on 5/5 phones

p0a.title: Send the fleet hold notice
p0a.do: Edit the draft in docs/program/notices/fleet-hold.md (fill the square-bracket words), send it to every technician (English and Urdu), then replace its status line with the date, channel and who it went to, keeping the text exactly as sent.
p0a.why: Opening, updating, uninstalling or tapping Discard on a phone can lose records that never reached the server.

p0a.title: Railway first: seal the old secret, cut old services off
p0a.do: Record the Railway project state. Copy the old FIXFLOW_JWT_SECRET from the Railway environment and seal it offline (never into this page). Then remove DATABASE_URL from, or scale to 0, any surviving service, and reset the Supabase database password in its dashboard. Record whether you can bind the old subdomain (H) and to what, and your account and billing access.
p0a.why: An old backend could otherwise drain phones or run its 02:30 pruner on the old data.
p0a.result: e.g. secret sealed yes; services cut 2/2; DB password reset yes; H = yes/no

p0a.title: Archive the R2 backups
p0a.do: Mint an R2 API token (type it only into your own terminal). List backups/db/, copy it to archive/pre-selfhost/, make a laptop copy in C:/fixflow-r2, then list the archive prefix and record both listings.
p0a.why: Backups can be pruned; this keeps a copy that nothing old can delete.
p0a.helper: r2-archive.sh (set AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in your own terminal first; never paste them here or into chat)
p0a.result: e.g. 31 files listed; archive listed 31; laptop copy yes

p0a.title: Supabase: take the dump and verify it, same day
p0a.do: Record status, pause date, the restore deadline shown, Postgres major version. If restorable: restore it and take the dump now through the session pooler, sha256 it, upload it to the R2 archive, and verify it the same day with design Appendix C. If only a dashboard download exists, convert it (see the plan). If unrecoverable: screenshot. 'Unknown' is not accepted, and 'project restored' alone is not enough.
p0a.why: The real data's last copy. Its restore deadline can run out; the recovery case (a/b/c) and P9-0b depend on it.
p0a.helper: supabase-dump.sh then verify-dump.sh (set FIXFLOW_SUPABASE_URL in your own terminal first; never paste it here or into chat)
p0a.result: e.g. restorable yes; PG 15; dump sha256 first 8 chars; Appendix C passed yes

p0a.title: Fleet roster
p0a.do: For each phone: which technician id, maker / model / Android version, and whether it is shared.
p0a.why: Every later phone step (drain, install, release) is per phone.
p0a.helper: phone-facts.sh (read-only on the phone: it never opens the app; needs adb and apksigner)

p0a.title: Field build facts, per phone
p0a.do: Pull each phone's installed app (adb), read its signing certificate (apksigner), versionCode, whether the bundle contains jobs.outbox.v2 (v2) and which API host it has baked in. Compare the certificate with the EAS keystore (K). Export the keystore.
p0a.why: K, H and v2 choose which drain branch each phone takes. The keystore cannot be re-made.
p0a.helper: phone-facts.sh (read-only on the phone: it never opens the app; needs adb and apksigner)
p0a.result: per phone: K yes/no, v2 yes/no, versionCode; keystore exported yes

p0a.title: Photos of what is stuck, per phone, today
p0a.do: Airplane mode on and Wi-Fi off, open FixFlow, photograph the clock screen's DID-NOT-SYNC list and every job banner, close the app, airplane mode off. 'Not reachable' only for a phone whose login is gone.
p0a.why: The only record of what each phone still holds if a drain cannot happen.

p0a.why: Confirms error tracking for the phones still works (decided: Sentry stays).

p0a.title: Decisions
p0a.do: Answer every decision row (the board further down) or leave it to its default. Includes the chain-anchor address and mail relay (or 'unanchored'), geofence thresholds, drain host, SDK spike, shift reminder, Odoo plan and version.

p0a.helper: the decisions board on this page

p0a.title: Cut the app's network, every phone
p0a.do: In system settings, turn off FixFlow's Wi-Fi and mobile data (or background data off plus Wi-Fi blocked by a named method, or airplane mode if nothing else works). Record method and date per phone.
p0a.why: Stops a phone sending to a wrong or old server. It lifts only per the plan's branch box.

p0a.title: Restrict the committed client keys
p0a.do: In the Maps, Firebase and Sentry consoles, restrict each client key to the app's package name and SHA-1. Record done per key.
p0a.why: These keys are in the code; restriction makes them useless elsewhere.
p0a.result: e.g. Maps yes, Firebase yes, Sentry yes

p0a.title: Workshop Wi-Fi facts
p0a.do: Does the workshop have Wi-Fi the technicians' phones join during shifts? Its name (SSID), the access point id(s) (BSSID), and which phones join it. 'No Wi-Fi' is a valid answer.
p0a.why: Feeds an attendance rule; 'no Wi-Fi' simply turns that rule off.
p0a.result: e.g. yes, SSID name, 1 BSSID, phones 1-4

p0a.title: Who holds cash in the field
p0a.do: Do technicians hold cash collected at customers, or receive online payments into personal wallets, before handing them to the shop? For how long, and who counts the hand-over?
p0a.why: Decides whether the accounting needs a cash-remittance source. 'Never: every rupee reaches the manager the same day' is valid.
p0a.result: e.g. yes, up to 2 days, manager counts

p0a.title: Books basis
p0a.do: Registered for sales tax (SRB/FBR)? Books on cash basis? Is there an accountant, and do they want per-transaction entries or periodic totals? A second money writer (counter POS, offline web, second shop) planned within 12 months?
p0a.why: Shapes the Odoo hand-off. Unknowns are answered later in P9-0b, not here.
p0a.result: e.g. not registered; cash; accountant yes, weekly totals; no

machine.docker: Docker's network address pools are used up by another project (29 networks). The gate scripts work around it: they share the database container's network, and anything needing a real network uses 10.77.0.0/16. FixFlow never prunes networks it did not create and never reconfigures Docker.

rules: No phone gets a new app until its stuck data has been drained and the after-check passed. Never uninstall, except in the one documented branch with your written sign-off per phone.
No claim that geofencing works without evidence from the fleet's own phone models.
During the drain the server runs one pinned image and nothing else.
The automatic WhatsApp dispatcher stays off until every phone is drained or retired.
The old Railway address may only hang (or, in one branch, proxy). It never answers on its own.
Technicians stay on hold until the written release notice.
Money is whole paisa; no money feed runs off the event cursor; the outbox never deletes a write.
